title.en: 4.1 Plug-ins: Transition, Modal, Scrollspy, Tab and Dropdown

body.en:
A Bootstrap plug-in is a ready-made JavaScript module that adds interactive behaviour to components: opening a modal, showing a dropdown menu, sliding a carousel, collapsing content, and so on.

Why plug-ins?

  • No custom JavaScript needed: most plug-ins work just by adding data attributes in HTML.
  • Saves development time and gives the same tested behaviour in all browsers.
  • Responsive and touch friendly (e.g. swipe in carousel).
  • Accessible: keyboard support, focus handling and ARIA attributes are built in.
  • Customisable through options, methods and events when needed.

Including plug-ins

All plug-ins are in one file, bootstrap.bundle.min.js, which also contains Popper (needed for dropdowns, tooltips and popovers). Place it at the end of the body. Bootstrap 5 does not need jQuery; Bootstrap 3 needed jQuery loaded first.

<!-- end of body: one file for all plug-ins -->
<script src="js/bootstrap.bundle.min.js"></script>
<!-- Bootstrap 3 needed jQuery first -->
<script src="js/jquery.min.js"></script>
<script src="js/bootstrap.min.js"></script>

List of plug-ins

Plug-inUse
TransitionHelper for CSS animations (built in since BS4)
ModalDialog box / pop-up window
DropdownToggleable menus
ScrollspyHighlights nav links while scrolling
TabSwitches tab panes
Tooltip / PopoverSmall hover labels / click boxes
AlertDismisses alert messages
ButtonToggle state of buttons
CollapseShows / hides content, accordion
CarouselImage slideshow
AffixFixes an element on scroll (BS3; now .sticky-top)

Bootstrap 5 also adds Offcanvas (side panel) and Toast (small notification).

h.en: Using Plug-ins: Data Attributes and JavaScript API

body.en:
Every Bootstrap plug-in can be used in two ways.

1. Data attributes (no code)

Add data-bs-toggle, data-bs-target, data-bs-dismiss, data-bs-ride etc. to HTML elements. Options can also be given as attributes, e.g. data-bs-interval="3000". In Bootstrap 3 the prefix was data- (data-toggle).

2. JavaScript API

  • Create: new bootstrap.Modal(element, options) or bootstrap.Modal.getOrCreateInstance(element).
  • Options: an object such as { backdrop: "static" }.
  • Methods: show(), hide(), toggle(), dispose() and plug-in-specific ones. Methods are asynchronous: they start the animation and return immediately.
  • Events: each plug-in fires custom events named action.bs.plugin. The infinitive form (show.bs.modal) fires at the start; the past participle (shown.bs.modal) fires after the animation. Calling e.preventDefault() in a start event cancels the action.
<!-- 1. data attributes -->
<button data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#box">
  Toggle</button>
<div class="collapse" id="box">...</div>
<script>
  // 2. JavaScript API
  var el = document.getElementById("box");
  var c = new bootstrap.Collapse(el, { toggle: false });
  c.show();                                 // method
  bootstrap.Collapse.getInstance(el);       // existing
  bootstrap.Collapse.getOrCreateInstance(el);
  el.addEventListener("shown.bs.collapse", function () {
    console.log("opened");                  // event
  });
</script>

Bootstrap 3 used jQuery syntax:

// Bootstrap 3 (jQuery)
$("#box").collapse("show");
$("#myModal").on("shown.bs.modal", function () { });

The transition plug-in (transition.js in Bootstrap 3) was a small helper that detected the end of CSS transitions (the transitionend event) so that other plug-ins could wait for animations. It was required by modal, carousel, collapse, alert and tab for their animations.

  • In Bootstrap 4/5 it is no longer a separate plug-in; the transition logic is built into each plug-in.
  • .fade gives an opacity transition; .show makes the element visible. Toggling .show fades an element in or out.
  • Animations: modal (fade and slide down), alert (fade out), collapse (.collapsing height change), carousel (.slide or .carousel-fade), tab panes (fade).
  • Custom transitions use the CSS transition property; JavaScript can react to transitionend.
  • Animations are switched off when the user's system has reduced motion enabled.
<div class="alert alert-info fade show" id="msg">Hello</div>
<script>
  msg.classList.toggle("show");   // fade out / in
  msg.addEventListener("transitionend", function () {
    console.log("finished");
  });
</script>

Smooth page transition (Practical 18)

Home, About and Contact can be placed as .tab-pane.fade sections in one page. Navbar links with data-bs-toggle="tab" switch them; the old page fades out and the new page fades in without reloading. Extra CSS (transform: translateY()) can add a slide effect.

<a class="nav-link active" data-bs-toggle="tab"
  href="#home">Home</a>
<a class="nav-link" data-bs-toggle="tab"
  href="#about">About</a>
<div class="tab-content">
  <section class="tab-pane fade show active" id="home">
    ...</section>
  <section class="tab-pane fade" id="about">...</section>
</div>

A modal is a dialog box (pop-up window) displayed on top of the current page. The page behind is covered by a dark backdrop and cannot be used until the modal is closed. Uses: confirmations (save, delete), login forms, messages, image previews.

<button class="btn btn-primary" data-bs-toggle="modal"
  data-bs-target="#info">Open</button>

<div class="modal fade" id="info" tabindex="-1">
  <div class="modal-dialog modal-dialog-centered">
    <div class="modal-content">
      <div class="modal-header">
        <h5 class="modal-title">Welcome</h5>
        <button class="btn-close" data-bs-dismiss="modal">
        </button>
      </div>
      <div class="modal-body">Results on 5 Dec.</div>
      <div class="modal-footer">
        <button class="btn btn-secondary"
          data-bs-dismiss="modal">Close</button>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

Structure

  • .modal (with .fade for animation, tabindex="-1") > .modal-dialog > .modal-content.
  • .modal-header (title + close button), .modal-body (content), .modal-footer (action buttons).

Opening and closing

  • Open: data-bs-toggle="modal" and data-bs-target="#id" on a button (or href on a link).
  • Close: any element with data-bs-dismiss="modal", a click on the backdrop, or the Esc key.

Variations

Class / attributeEffect
.modal-sm / .modal-lg / .modal-xlSmall (300 px) / large (800 px) / extra large (1140 px)
.modal-fullscreen, .modal-fullscreen-md-downFull screen (always / below md)
.modal-dialog-centeredVertically centred
.modal-dialog-scrollableOnly the body scrolls for long content
data-bs-backdrop="static"Does not close on an outside click
data-bs-keyboard="false"Does not close with Esc

Only one modal should be open at a time. Place the modal HTML at the top level of the body.

Properties (options)

OptionDefaultMeaning
backdroptruetrue = dark backdrop that closes the modal on click; false = no backdrop; "static" = backdrop that does not close it
keyboardtrueClose the modal with the Esc key
focustruePut the focus on the modal when opened

(Bootstrap 3 also had show and remote options.)

Methods

  • show(), hide(), toggle(): open, close, switch.
  • handleUpdate(): re-adjust the position if the height changes while open.
  • dispose(): destroys the modal object.
  • getInstance(el), getOrCreateInstance(el): static methods to get the object.

Events

EventFires
show.bs.modalWhen show is called (before opening); e.relatedTarget = the clicked button
shown.bs.modalAfter the modal is fully visible
hide.bs.modalWhen hide is called
hidden.bs.modalAfter the modal is fully hidden
hidePrevented.bs.modalWhen a static backdrop is clicked or Esc is pressed with keyboard false
var el = document.getElementById("info");
var m = new bootstrap.Modal(el, {
  backdrop: "static",     // no close on outside click
  keyboard: false         // no close on Esc
});
m.show();
el.addEventListener("show.bs.modal", function (e) {
  var opener = e.relatedTarget;    // button clicked
});
el.addEventListener("hidden.bs.modal", function () {
  console.log("closed");
});

Practical 19: a "Save record confirmation" modal opens when the form is submitted and adds the row only after "Yes"; a "Delete record confirmation" modal shows the name of the row and removes it after "Delete".

Scrollspy automatically updates the active link in a navigation (nav, navbar or list group) according to the section of the page that is currently visible while scrolling. It shows the user where they are in a long page.

<nav id="menu">
  <ul class="nav nav-pills">
    <li class="nav-item"><a class="nav-link" href="#s1">One</a></li>
    <li class="nav-item"><a class="nav-link" href="#s2">Two</a></li>
  </ul>
</nav>
<div data-bs-spy="scroll" data-bs-target="#menu"
  data-bs-smooth-scroll="true" tabindex="0"
  style="height: 300px; overflow-y: auto">
  <h4 id="s1">One</h4><p>...</p>
  <h4 id="s2">Two</h4><p>...</p>
</div>

Requirements

  • Add data-bs-spy="scroll" to the scrolling element (body or a div) and data-bs-target pointing to the nav.
  • Each nav link href="#id" must match the id of a section; the target nav must be visible.
  • A scrolling div needs a fixed height, overflow-y: auto and tabindex="0".

Options, method and event

  • Options: smoothScroll (smooth scrolling on link click), rootMargin and threshold (when a section counts as visible), target. Bootstrap 3/4 used offset (pixels from the top).
  • Method: refresh() after adding or removing sections; dispose().
  • Event: activate.bs.scrollspy fires when a new link becomes active (e.relatedTarget = that link).

Uses: long articles, documentation, single-page websites, news stories (Practical 20).

The tab plug-in makes tabs, pills or list groups switch between content panes without loading a new page (see Unit 3 for the nav styles).

  • Links get data-bs-toggle="tab", "pill" or "list", and point to a pane with href or data-bs-target.
  • Panes are .tab-pane inside .tab-content; the first has .active (and .show with .fade).

Methods

  • bootstrap.Tab.getOrCreateInstance(link).show(): activates the tab and shows its pane.
  • dispose(), getInstance().
var link = document.querySelector('a[href="#about"]');
bootstrap.Tab.getOrCreateInstance(link).show();

link.addEventListener("shown.bs.tab", function (e) {
  // e.target = new tab, e.relatedTarget = previous tab
});

Events (order)

  1. hide.bs.tab on the current tab
  2. show.bs.tab on the new tab
  3. hidden.bs.tab on the previous tab
  4. shown.bs.tab on the new tab

e.target is the active tab and e.relatedTarget the previous one. Uses: product details, unit summaries, settings pages, and the page switch of Practical 18.

The dropdown plug-in toggles a .dropdown-menu when the button with data-bs-toggle="dropdown" is clicked. It uses Popper to place the menu so that it stays inside the screen.

Options

OptionMeaning
autoClosetrue (any click closes), "inside", "outside", false (only the toggle closes it)
offsetDistance of the menu, e.g. "0,10"
boundary / referenceArea for overflow checking / element used for positioning
display"dynamic" (Popper) or "static"

Methods and events

  • Methods: toggle(), show(), hide(), update() (re-position), dispose().
  • Events: show.bs.dropdown, shown.bs.dropdown, hide.bs.dropdown, hidden.bs.dropdown (fired on the toggle element).
  • Keyboard: up/down arrows move through the items; Esc closes.
<button class="btn btn-success dropdown-toggle"
  data-bs-toggle="dropdown" data-bs-auto-close="outside"
  data-bs-offset="0,10">Filters</button>
<script>
  var dd = bootstrap.Dropdown.getOrCreateInstance(btn);
  dd.toggle();
  btn.addEventListener("hidden.bs.dropdown", function () {
    console.log("menu closed");
  });
</script>

title.en: 4.2 Tooltip, Popover, Alert, Button, Collapse, Carousel and Affix

body.en:
A tooltip is a small label that appears when the user hovers over or focuses on an element. The text comes from the title (or data-bs-title) attribute.

<button class="btn btn-secondary" data-bs-toggle="tooltip"
  data-bs-placement="top" title="Save the form">Save</button>
<script>
  var sel = '[data-bs-toggle="tooltip"]';
  document.querySelectorAll(sel).forEach(function (el) {
    new bootstrap.Tooltip(el);
  });
</script>
  • Tooltips are opt-in: for performance they must be initialised with JavaScript (new bootstrap.Tooltip(el)).
  • They depend on Popper (use the bundle file).
  • Empty titles show no tooltip. For disabled buttons, put the tooltip on a wrapper span with tabindex="0".

Options

placement (top, right, bottom, left, auto), trigger ("hover focus", "click", "focus", "manual"), html (allow HTML), title, delay, animation, offset, container, customClass.

Methods

show(), hide(), toggle(), enable(), disable(), toggleEnabled(), setContent(), update(), dispose().

Events

EventFires
show.bs.tooltipWhen show starts
shown.bs.tooltipAfter the tooltip is visible
hide.bs.tooltip / hidden.bs.tooltipWhen hiding starts / ends
inserted.bs.tooltipAfter the tooltip element is added to the page
var t = new bootstrap.Tooltip(btn, {
  placement: "bottom", trigger: "click", html: true,
  title: "<b>Bold</b> tip", delay: { show: 200, hide: 100 }
});
t.show();  t.hide();  t.toggle();  t.disable();
btn.addEventListener("shown.bs.tooltip", function () { });

A popover is a larger pop-up box with a title and content, opened by a click by default. It is built on the tooltip plug-in.

<button class="btn btn-danger" data-bs-toggle="popover"
  data-bs-title="Last date"
  data-bs-content="Fees by 30 Nov.">Click me</button>
<a tabindex="0" class="btn btn-warning" role="button"
  data-bs-toggle="popover" data-bs-trigger="focus"
  data-bs-content="Closes on next click">Dismissible</a>
<script>
  document.querySelectorAll('[data-bs-toggle="popover"]')
    .forEach(function (el) { new bootstrap.Popover(el); });
</script>
  • Attributes: data-bs-toggle="popover", data-bs-title, data-bs-content, data-bs-placement, data-bs-trigger.
  • Popovers are opt-in and need Popper, like tooltips.
  • Dismiss on next click: data-bs-trigger="focus" on an <a> with tabindex="0".
  • Options: same as tooltip plus content. Methods: show(), hide(), toggle(), enable(), disable(), setContent(), dispose(). Events: show/shown/hide/hidden/inserted.bs.popover.
TooltipPopover
Short text onlyTitle and content (can be HTML)
Hover / focusClick (default)
Small black labelWhite box with header

Practical 20 uses scrollspy for the story sections, tooltips on photos, collapse for "Read more" and popovers for the reporter and fare details.

Alert plug-in

The alert plug-in makes alerts dismissible. A close button with data-bs-dismiss="alert" removes the alert from the page (with a fade when .fade .show are present).

<div class="alert alert-warning alert-dismissible fade show"
  id="note">Holiday on Monday.
  <button class="btn-close" data-bs-dismiss="alert"></button>
</div>
<script>
  bootstrap.Alert.getOrCreateInstance(note).close();
  note.addEventListener("closed.bs.alert", function () {
    console.log("alert removed");
  });
</script>
  • Methods: close() (fade out and remove), dispose(), getInstance(), getOrCreateInstance().
  • Events: close.bs.alert (close called) and closed.bs.alert (alert removed); used to show a message after closing.

Button plug-in

The button plug-in controls the state of buttons.

<button class="btn btn-outline-primary"
  data-bs-toggle="button">Like</button>
<input type="checkbox" class="btn-check" id="c1">
<label class="btn btn-outline-success" for="c1">Hostel</label>
<script>
  bootstrap.Button.getOrCreateInstance(likeBtn).toggle();
</script>
  • Toggle button: data-bs-toggle="button" switches the .active class and aria-pressed on every click. Method: toggle().
  • Checkbox / radio buttons: in Bootstrap 5, input.btn-check with label.btn; in Bootstrap 3, data-toggle="buttons" on a btn-group.
  • Loading state: Bootstrap 3 had $(btn).button("loading") with data-loading-text, and button("reset"). In Bootstrap 5, disable the button and add a .spinner-border-sm using JavaScript.

The collapse plug-in shows and hides content with a smooth height animation. It is used for "Read more" sections, FAQs, accordions and the responsive navbar menu.

<a class="btn btn-primary" data-bs-toggle="collapse"
  href="#more">Read more</a>
<button class="btn btn-success" data-bs-toggle="collapse"
  data-bs-target=".multi">Toggle both</button>
<div class="collapse" id="more">Extra text...</div>
<div class="collapse multi">A</div>
<div class="collapse multi">B</div>

How it works

  • Hidden content has .collapse; while animating it gets .collapsing; when visible it has .collapse.show.
  • Trigger: data-bs-toggle="collapse" on a link (href) or button (data-bs-target). A class selector controls multiple targets.
  • .collapse-horizontal animates width instead of height.

Properties, methods and events

TypeMembers
Optionsparent: selector; when one item opens, others in the parent close (accordion). toggle: toggle on creation (default true)
Methodsshow(), hide(), toggle(), dispose(), getInstance(), getOrCreateInstance()
Eventsshow.bs.collapse, shown.bs.collapse, hide.bs.collapse, hidden.bs.collapse
var c = new bootstrap.Collapse("#more", {
  toggle: false,          // do not open on creation
  parent: "#faq"          // accordion behaviour
});
c.show();  c.hide();  c.toggle();
more.addEventListener("hidden.bs.collapse", function () {
  console.log("closed");
});

Accordion

An accordion is a group of collapsible items where only one is open at a time, using data-bs-parent.

<div class="accordion" id="faq">
  <div class="accordion-item">
    <h2 class="accordion-header">
      <button class="accordion-button" data-bs-toggle="collapse"
        data-bs-target="#q1">Who can apply?</button>
    </h2>
    <div id="q1" class="accordion-collapse collapse show"
      data-bs-parent="#faq">
      <div class="accordion-body">SSC passed.</div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <!-- more .accordion-item ... -->
</div>

A carousel is a slideshow that cycles through images, text or other content, with optional controls, indicators and captions.

<div id="g" class="carousel slide" data-bs-ride="carousel"
  data-bs-interval="3000">
  <div class="carousel-indicators">
    <button data-bs-target="#g" data-bs-slide-to="0"
      class="active"></button>
    <button data-bs-target="#g" data-bs-slide-to="1"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="carousel-inner">
    <div class="carousel-item active">
      <img src="img/1.jpg" class="d-block w-100" alt="One">
      <div class="carousel-caption">
        <h5>Rani ki Vav</h5><p>Patan</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="carousel-item">
      <img src="img/2.jpg" class="d-block w-100" alt="Two">
    </div>
  </div>
  <button class="carousel-control-prev" data-bs-target="#g"
    data-bs-slide="prev">
    <span class="carousel-control-prev-icon"></span></button>
  <button class="carousel-control-next" data-bs-target="#g"
    data-bs-slide="next">
    <span class="carousel-control-next-icon"></span></button>
</div>

Parts

  • .carousel.slide: wrapper with an id; data-bs-ride="carousel" starts auto-play on load.
  • .carousel-inner > .carousel-item: the slides; one must have .active.
  • .carousel-caption: text over the image.
  • .carousel-indicators: small bars to jump to a slide (data-bs-slide-to).
  • .carousel-control-prev / -next: arrows (data-bs-slide="prev"/"next").

Options, methods and events

TypeMembers
Optionsinterval (ms, default 5000), ride, pause ("hover"), wrap (loop), keyboard, touch (swipe)
Methodscycle(), pause(), prev(), next(), nextWhenVisible(), to(n), dispose()
Eventsslide.bs.carousel (start), slid.bs.carousel (end); e.from, e.to, e.direction
var car = bootstrap.Carousel.getOrCreateInstance("#g");
car.to(3);   car.pause();   car.cycle();
car.next();  car.prev();
g.addEventListener("slid.bs.carousel", function (e) {
  count.textContent = "Photo " + (e.to + 1);
});
  • .carousel-fade fades between slides instead of sliding; .carousel-dark gives dark controls (BS 5.3: data-bs-theme="dark").
  • data-bs-interval on a single item sets its own time.
  • Give all images the same size (or fixed height with object-fit: cover) so the carousel does not jump.

Practical 21 builds an animated gallery of seven photos with indicators, captions, a fade switch, pause/play and thumbnails.

The affix plug-in (Bootstrap 3) fixed an element, such as a navbar or side menu, in place after the page was scrolled past a certain point. Before that point the element scrolled normally.

  • Usage: data-spy="affix" with data-offset-top="200" (and data-offset-bottom).
  • The plug-in switched classes: .affix-top (before the offset), .affix (fixed), .affix-bottom (near the bottom). The developer wrote CSS for these classes.
  • Events: affix.bs.affix, affixed.bs.affix, affix-top.bs.affix, etc.

Bootstrap 4/5 replacement

The affix plug-in was removed in Bootstrap 4 because CSS position: sticky gives the same result without JavaScript.

<!-- Bootstrap 3 -->
<nav class="navbar" data-spy="affix" data-offset-top="200">
<!-- Bootstrap 5 -->
<nav class="navbar sticky-top bg-dark">...</nav>
<style>
  .side { position: sticky; top: 70px; }
</style>
  • .sticky-top: the element scrolls with the page until it reaches the top, then sticks there.
  • .sticky-{sm|md|lg|xl|xxl}-top: sticky only from that breakpoint; .sticky-bottom sticks at the bottom.
  • .fixed-top: always fixed (not the same as affix).
  • For extra effects (shadow, smaller logo), a scroll event listener can add a class when scrollY passes an offset.

title.en: Using a plug-in two ways: data attributes and JavaScript

code.en:
Bootstrap plug-ins

Opened by data-bs-toggle="collapse".
Opened by JavaScript methods.

Event log

programs.out:
The page shows "Bootstrap version: 5.3.3".
"Toggle with data attribute" opens and closes the first box without any JavaScript code.
The show(), hide() and toggle() buttons control the second box through JavaScript.
Each time a box finishes opening or closing, a line such as "shown.bs.collapse on #box2" is added to the event log.

expl.en:
• Every Bootstrap plug-in can be used in two ways:
    1. Data attributes (no code): data-bs-toggle, data-bs-target, and options as data-bs-*.
    2. JavaScript API: new bootstrap.Collapse(el, options) or bootstrap.Collapse.getOrCreateInstance(el), then call methods.
  • Options are passed as an object, here { toggle: false } so the box does not open on creation.
  • Methods such as show(), hide(), toggle(), dispose() control the plug-in.
  • Events are named action.bs.plugin: the present form (show) fires at the start and the past form (shown) after the animation ends.
  • All plug-ins are in bootstrap.bundle.min.js, which includes Popper (needed for dropdowns, tooltips and popovers). Bootstrap 5 does not need jQuery.

title.en: Transition: fade classes and the transitionend event

code.en:
Bootstrap transitions

1. .fade and .show

I fade in and out with Bootstrap's .fade class.

2. Custom CSS transition

Box

Waiting...

programs.out:
A blue info alert with a "Fade out" button. Clicking it fades the alert smoothly to invisible, and the button changes to "Fade in".
"Move box" slides the green box to the right, changing its colour to purple. After the movement the text reads "Transition finished: margin-left" (or background-color).

expl.en:
• Transition plug-in (Bootstrap 3: transition.js) was a helper used by other plug-ins (modal, carousel, collapse, alert) to detect the end of CSS transitions. In Bootstrap 5 it is built into every plug-in and is not used separately.
  • .fade sets transition: opacity .15s linear and opacity 0; adding .show makes opacity 1. Toggling .show gives a fade effect.
  • Animated components: modal (fade + slide), alert (fade on close), collapse (.collapsing height animation), carousel (slide or .carousel-fade), tab panes (fade).
  • Custom effects use the CSS transition property; the transitionend event tells JavaScript when it finished.
  • Bootstrap respects the user's prefers-reduced-motion setting and turns animations off.

title.en: Smooth page transition: Home, About and Contact (Practical 18)

code.en:
GreenTech
  • Home
  • About
  • Contact

Welcome to GreenTech

Solar solutions for homes in Gujarat.

About us

Started in 2015 in Surat, we have installed solar panels on more than 2,000 roofs.

Mission Clean energy for every home.
Team 40 trained engineers.

Contact us

programs.out:
A blue navbar with the brand "GreenTech" and the links Home, About and Contact.
The Home page shows a grey welcome box with a "Contact us" button.
Clicking About or Contact (or the "Contact us" button) makes the current page fade out, and the new page fades in while sliding up slightly, without reloading. About shows two cards (Mission, Team); Contact shows a form with Name, Mobile, Message and Send.

expl.en:
• The three "pages" are .tab-pane sections in one .tab-content, so changing page needs no reload.
  • The navbar links use the tab plug-in: data-bs-toggle="tab" with href="#id".
  • The transition comes from .fade on each pane: Bootstrap waits for the old pane to fade out before showing the new one (transition end detection).
  • Custom CSS adds transform: translateY(25px) to make the page slide up while fading in.
  • bootstrap.Tab.getOrCreateInstance(link).show() opens a page from a button.
  • navbar-expand keeps the menu always expanded because it has only three short links.

title.en: Modal dialog: basic, centred, large scrollable and static

code.en:
Modal dialog boxes

Welcome
Results will be declared on 5 Dec.
Exam rules

Session expired. Please log in again.

programs.out:
Three buttons. "Basic (centred)" opens a dialog in the middle of the screen with the title "Welcome", the text "Results will be declared on 5 Dec." and a Close button; the page behind becomes dark.
"Large + scrollable" opens a wide dialog "Exam rules" with 25 rules; only the body scrolls while the header and the "I agree" button stay visible.
"Static backdrop" opens a small dialog "Session expired" that does not close on an outside click or the Esc key, only with "Log in".

expl.en:
• Modal structure: .modal.fade > .modal-dialog > .modal-content > .modal-header / .modal-body / .modal-footer.
  • Open: a button with data-bs-toggle="modal" and data-bs-target="#id". Close: any element with data-bs-dismiss="modal", a click on the backdrop, or Esc.
  • Sizes: .modal-sm (300 px), default (500 px), .modal-lg (800 px), .modal-xl (1140 px), .modal-fullscreen or .modal-fullscreen-md-down.
  • Position: .modal-dialog-centered; long content: .modal-dialog-scrollable.
  • Static backdrop: data-bs-backdrop="static" and data-bs-keyboard="false".
  • tabindex="-1" lets the modal take keyboard focus.

code.en:
Student list

  • Ravi Patel
  • Priya Shah

Event log

programs.out:

expl.en:
• Options (object or data-bs-*): backdrop (true / false / "static"), keyboard (Esc closes), focus.
  • Methods: show(), hide(), toggle(), handleUpdate() (re-position), dispose(); static bootstrap.Modal.getInstance(el) and getOrCreateInstance(el).

  • Methods: show(), hide(), toggle(), enable(), disable(), toggleEnabled(), setContent(), update(), dispose().

expl.en:
• Collapse shows and hides content with a height animation. The content gets .collapse (hidden), .collapsing (during animation) and .collapse.show (visible).

expl.en:
• A carousel is a slideshow that cycles through images or content.

q.en: What is a Bootstrap plug-in?

a.en: A ready-made JavaScript module that adds interactive behaviour (modal, dropdown, carousel, collapse ...) to components.

q.en: Why use Bootstrap plug-ins?

a.en: No custom JavaScript is needed, they save time, work in all browsers, are responsive, accessible and customisable.

q.en: Which file contains all Bootstrap 5 plug-ins?

a.en: bootstrap.bundle.min.js (includes Popper).

q.en: What is Popper used for?

a.en: Positioning dropdowns, tooltips and popovers.

q.en: Does Bootstrap 5 need jQuery?

a.en: No. Bootstrap 3 and 4 needed jQuery; Bootstrap 5 uses plain JavaScript.

q.en: What are the two ways to use a plug-in?

a.en: Data attributes in HTML, or the JavaScript API (new bootstrap.X(el, options) and methods).

q.en: What is the difference between show.bs.modal and shown.bs.modal?

a.en: show fires when opening starts; shown fires after the animation has finished.

q.en: How do you stop a modal from opening in an event?

a.en: Call e.preventDefault() in the show.bs.modal handler.

q.en: What is getOrCreateInstance()?

a.en: A static method that returns the existing plug-in object of an element or creates a new one.

q.en: What was the transition plug-in?

a.en: A Bootstrap 3 helper (transition.js) that detected the end of CSS transitions for other plug-ins; built into each plug-in since Bootstrap 4.

q.en: What do .fade and .show do?

a.en: .fade adds an opacity transition and hides the element; .show makes it visible.

q.en: What is a modal?

a.en: A dialog box shown on top of the page with a dark backdrop.

q.en: Name the parts of a modal.

a.en: .modal > .modal-dialog > .modal-content with .modal-header, .modal-body and .modal-footer.

q.en: How do you open a modal without JavaScript?

a.en: A button with data-bs-toggle="modal" and data-bs-target="#id".

q.en: How do you close a modal?

a.en: An element with data-bs-dismiss="modal", the Esc key, a backdrop click, or the hide() method.

q.en: What is a static backdrop?

a.en: data-bs-backdrop="static": the modal does not close when clicking outside it.

q.en: Name the modal sizes.

a.en: .modal-sm, default, .modal-lg, .modal-xl and .modal-fullscreen.

q.en: List the modal options.

a.en: backdrop, keyboard and focus.

q.en: List the modal methods.

a.en: show(), hide(), toggle(), handleUpdate(), dispose().

q.en: List the modal events.

a.en: show.bs.modal, shown.bs.modal, hide.bs.modal, hidden.bs.modal, hidePrevented.bs.modal.

q.en: What is e.relatedTarget in show.bs.modal?

a.en: The button that was clicked to open the modal.

q.en: What is scrollspy?

a.en: A plug-in that updates the active nav link according to the section visible while scrolling.

q.en: Which attributes start scrollspy?

a.en: data-bs-spy="scroll" and data-bs-target="#nav" on the scrolling element.

q.en: Which event does scrollspy fire?

a.en: activate.bs.scrollspy.

q.en: When is the scrollspy refresh() method used?

a.en: After sections are added to or removed from the page.

q.en: How do you show a tab from JavaScript?

a.en: bootstrap.Tab.getOrCreateInstance(link).show().

q.en: List the tab events in order.

a.en: hide.bs.tab, show.bs.tab, hidden.bs.tab, shown.bs.tab.

q.en: What does the dropdown autoClose option do?

a.en: Decides which clicks close the menu: true, "inside", "outside" or false.

q.en: List the dropdown events.

a.en: show.bs.dropdown, shown.bs.dropdown, hide.bs.dropdown, hidden.bs.dropdown.

q.en: What is a tooltip?

a.en: A small label shown on hover or focus, taken from the title attribute.

q.en: Why must tooltips be initialised with JavaScript?

a.en: They are opt-in for performance reasons: new bootstrap.Tooltip(el).

q.en: Name the tooltip placements.

a.en: top, right, bottom, left and auto.

q.en: List the tooltip methods.

a.en: show(), hide(), toggle(), enable(), disable(), toggleEnabled(), setContent(), update(), dispose().

q.en: List the tooltip events.

a.en: show.bs.tooltip, shown.bs.tooltip, hide.bs.tooltip, hidden.bs.tooltip, inserted.bs.tooltip.

q.en: How do you show a tooltip on a disabled button?

a.en: Put the tooltip on a wrapper span with tabindex="0".

q.en: Difference between a tooltip and a popover?

a.en: A tooltip shows short text on hover; a popover has a title and content and opens on click.

q.en: How do you make a popover close on the next click?

a.en: Use data-bs-trigger="focus" on an <a> with tabindex="0".

q.en: What does the alert plug-in do?

a.en: Closes alerts with data-bs-dismiss="alert" or the close() method.

q.en: Which event fires after an alert is closed?

a.en: closed.bs.alert.

q.en: What does data-bs-toggle="button" do?

a.en: Makes a toggle button that switches the .active class and aria-pressed.

q.en: How was the loading state of a button made in Bootstrap 3?

a.en: $(btn).button("loading") with data-loading-text; in Bootstrap 5, disable it and add a spinner with JavaScript.

q.en: What is the collapse plug-in?

a.en: It shows and hides content with a height animation.

q.en: Which classes does collapse use?

a.en: .collapse (hidden), .collapsing (animating) and .collapse.show (visible).

q.en: List the collapse options.

a.en: parent and toggle.

q.en: List the collapse events.

a.en: show.bs.collapse, shown.bs.collapse, hide.bs.collapse, hidden.bs.collapse.

q.en: How does an accordion keep only one item open?

a.en: Each collapse has data-bs-parent pointing to the accordion.

q.en: What is a carousel?

a.en: A slideshow that cycles through images or content.

q.en: Which attribute starts a carousel automatically?

a.en: data-bs-ride="carousel" (time set with data-bs-interval).

q.en: What are carousel indicators?

a.en: Small bars or dots that show the current slide and jump to a slide with data-bs-slide-to.

q.en: List the carousel methods.

a.en: cycle(), pause(), prev(), next(), nextWhenVisible(), to(n), dispose().

q.en: Which carousel event fires after a slide changes?

a.en: slid.bs.carousel (slide.bs.carousel at the start); e.to gives the new index.

q.en: How do you make a carousel fade?

a.en: Add .carousel-fade to the .carousel.

q.en: What was the affix plug-in?

a.en: A Bootstrap 3 plug-in that fixed an element after scrolling past an offset (data-spy="affix" data-offset-top).

q.en: What replaces affix in Bootstrap 5?

a.en: CSS position: sticky through .sticky-top (and .sticky-bottom).

q.en: Difference between .fixed-top and .sticky-top?

a.en: .fixed-top is always fixed; .sticky-top scrolls normally until it reaches the top, then sticks.
